I have farmed this land for many years. The rains here in the North East are not as plenty as they once were, so I must use fertilizer to help my sorghum grow well — I will buy a bag of NPK and some urea if I can manage it, and spread it carefully. I also keep a few goats, so I will carry their manure to the plot before planting. The seed I will save from last year as I always do, my own sorghum is good enough; improved seed costs too much and I trust what I know. I am old now, so my sons and grandchildren will help with weeding, but I will hire a few young men for the heavy clearing at the start.
